name: Middleby Corporation
reason: Roll-up of foodservice/food-processing/residential kitchen brands (acquisitions ~0.88x 10y FCF, net debt/EBITDA 3.0x) now mid-breakup into separate companies, with adjusted EPS 6.75 down to 0.86x the 2023 peak; too much portfolio change to forecast 5-10 years out.

name: U.S. Bancorp
reason: Fifth-largest US bank with a low-cost national deposit base plus a payments/trust fee franchise, minimal acquisition spend outside Union Bank and falling shares (-1.3%/yr); 10y adjusted EPS CAGR only 3.9% after the 2022-23 rate/AOCI hit, but EPS is recovering (4.62 in 2025, consensus +14% FY1, LTG ~10%) at ~10x NTM EPS - worth deep work on whether pre-2020 compounding returns.

name: PENN Entertainment, Inc.
reason: Regional casino operator with three straight years of losses (EPS -5.83 in 2025) from failed online-betting bets, EBIT margin 3.9% vs 21% peak, net debt/EBITDA 14.7x including lease obligations and shares up 4.8%/yr; fails the balance-sheet and predictability tests.

name: AllianceBernstein Holding L.P.
reason: Active asset manager whose fee earnings track market levels and fund flows (EPS fell 24% in 2022) against a secular shift to passive; 10y EPS CAGR 5.9% and payout of nearly all earnings leave no clear route to >=7% growth.

name: Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc.
reason: Profits depend mainly on one drug, Ingrezza, which was picked for Medicare price negotiation with lower prices from 2027, while growth relies on the newly launched Crenessity and the pipeline; strong balance sheet (net cash) but outcomes are binary.

name: Textron Inc.
reason: Diversified aerospace/defense conglomerate with revenue CAGR of just 1.0% over 10y and EBIT margin 6.8% (10y avg 7.2%); EPS growth of 9.3%/yr came almost entirely from buybacks (shares -4.3%/yr, buybacks 1.06x FCF) and EPS sits at its 10y high - ordinary business, not special.

name: Peoples Bancorp Inc.
reason: Acquisitive Ohio community bank: shares up 7.2%/yr over 10y, 10y avg ROE only 8.1%, and EPS of 3.18 is 0.75x the 2023 peak; growth has come from M&A, not organic franchise strength.

name: Teleflex Incorporated
reason: Acquisition-built medtech (acquisitions 1.15x 10y FCF) with adjusted EPS halved to 6.98 in 2025, EBIT margin at a 10y low of 13.9%, net debt/EBITDA 5.1x and a portfolio breakup underway; a GAAP vs adjusted gap of ~257% also points to low earnings quality.

name: Group 1 Automotive, Inc.
reason: Cyclical auto dealer whose EPS jumped from 10.93 (2019) to 45.71 (2022) on pandemic-era vehicle pricing and is now fading (consensus -9% FY1, LTG -3%); growth has been driven by acquisitions (1.25x FCF) and net debt/EBITDA is 5.5x including floorplan debt.

name: Lakeland Financial Corporation
reason: Well-run, conservatively capitalised Indiana commercial bank (10y avg ROE 14.5%, flat share count, no acquisitions), but EPS is at 0.99x its 10y high and consensus FY2-FY3 growth is only ~3-4%/yr after recent commercial credit losses; a good bank with no route to >=7% growth.

name: Interface, Inc.
reason: Carpet tile maker selling into the cyclical office renovation market, with EPS at 1.0x and EBIT margin at 100th percentile of its 10y history (11.8%) after a sharp run-up, revenue CAGR 3.3% and GAAP/adjusted gap ~69%; cyclical peak and no clear moat.

name: Valley National Bancorp
reason: Acquisition-driven NJ/NY/FL bank (shares up 9.2%/yr over 10y) heavily concentrated in commercial real estate, with 10y avg ROE 8.0% and EPS cut 41% in 2024 on credit and funding costs; fails the organic-growth and credit-quality tests.

name: J.M. Smucker Company
reason: Packaged-food company with coffee commodity exposure, 10y EPS CAGR 4.3% (0.1% over 5y), the levered Hostess deal (net debt/EBITDA 3.3x, 10y ROIC 3.3%) and volume pressure from GLP-1 drugs and private label; ordinary returns with no route to >=7% growth.

name: Silgan Holdings Inc.
reason: Steady rigid-packaging operator with good capital allocation, but its 9.6% 10y EPS CAGR was largely bought (acquisitions 1.07x 10y FCF), net debt/EBITDA is 3.6x, and organic growth in metal food cans is low single digits; growth comes from leverage and M&A, not the core business.

name: Commercial Metals Company
reason: Rebar/steel minimill producer whose earnings follow steel spreads (EPS 8.19 in 2022, 3.13 in 2025, 6.82 FY26) with acquisitions 1.44x FCF and consensus FY2-FY3 EPS falling; commodity cyclical.

name: Willis Lease Finance Corporation
reason: Aircraft engine lessor with leverage-funded growth (net debt/EBITDA 6.6x, 10y FCF conversion negative) whose EPS is at 1.0x its 10y high after near-zero 2021-22; spread and aviation-cycle dependent.

name: Coeur Mining, Inc.
reason: Precious-metals miner whose earnings depend on gold/silver prices: EPS and EBIT margin (36.3%) are at 10y highs after years of losses, shares are up 16.8%/yr and 10y avg ROIC is -1.5%.

name: Biogen Inc.
reason: Neurology biotech facing patent cliffs: adjusted EPS of 15.28 is 0.45x the 2020 peak as the MS franchise (Tecfidera) lost exclusivity, and replacements like Leqembi and Skyclarys are uncertain; consensus LTG is ~1.4%.

name: Alliance Resource Partners, L.P.
reason: Thermal coal producer facing secular utility retirements, with earnings set by coal/oil-gas prices (EPS 4.81 in 2023 to 2.40 in 2025, 10y EPS CAGR 1.3%); commodity with structural decline.

name: World Kinect Corporation
reason: Fuel distributor with 0.7% EBIT margin, ~0% 10y avg ROIC and 10y EPS CAGR of -3.2%, exposed to fuel price volatility and the energy transition, plus a ~62% GAAP/adjusted gap; low-value-added middleman.
